sentences.text: Antarctilamna was an extinct genus of cartilaginous fish that possessed robust spines located in front of the first dorsal fin lacking a deep insertion area.
The fish had distinctive diplodont teeth featuring small intermediate cusps.
Antarctilamna ultima is the first recorded Devonian cartilaginous fish known from a juvenile specimen.
The juvenile status of this individual is supported by its small size and a head and branchial region exceeding a quarter of its body length.
The genus Antarctilamna was described by Young in 1982.
Fossils of Antarctilamna have been discovered in Antarctica and Australia.
The description of Antarctilamna prisca is based on material from both Antarctic and New South Wales localities.
The most recently occurring species, Antarctilamna ultima, was found at the Waterloo Farm lagerstätte in South Africa.
Antarctilamna ultima is described from an individual approximately 1 meter long.
Estimates suggest Antarctilamna ultima could have reached several meters in length.
Studies suggest large sharks may have entered the Waterloo Farm estuary to forage, though it is also possible they gave birth there, using the lake at the Waterloo Farm lagerstätte as a nursery.
Antarctilamna belongs to the class Chondrichthyes.
The parent group of Antarctilamna is the family Antarctilamnidae.
It is debated whether Antarctilamna is related to xenacanths or represents a basal chondrichthyan.
Antarctilamna lived from the Lochkovian to the Famennian stages, between 419.62 and 358.86 million years ago.
The genus includes two species: Antarctilamna prisca and Antarctilamna ultima.
